news.title: 巴克莱削减人力并加大AI投入
news.snippet: 继渣打银行之后，巴克莱将部分支出转向AI，同时裁员以降低成本，反映金融业AI投资趋势。
news.raw_snippet:
Oct 16

Standard Chartered said in May that it was “scaling practical uses of automation, advanced analytics and artificial intelligence to streamline processes, improve decision‑making and enhance both client service and internal efficiency.”

The cryptocurrency trading platform is cutting approximately 14% of its workforce partly due to AI.

In a blog post, CEO Brian Armstrong said that AI was changing the way that Coinbase worked. [...] “The core thesis is simple. Intelligence tools have changed what it means to build and run a company,” Jack Dorsey said in a letter to shareholders in Block, the parent company to online payment platforms such as Square and Cash App. “A significantly smaller team, using the tools we’re building, can do more and do it better,” he said.

Dorsey’s comments explicitly naming AI as a key driver behind the decision were also posted on X, or Twitter, a company he co-founded. [...] Kroger said last week that it will lay off 3,000 corporate employees over the next three years as the national grocery chain ramps up its use of artificial intelligence.

“Technology is reshaping what’s possible,” CEO Greg Foran wrote in a memo to employees. “The way work gets done is changing across every industry; we must adapt and take advantage of technology. We need to adopt capabilities, reduce duplicative work and look closely at where work is best fit to be done.”

news.raw_snippet:

Bill Gates warned that artificial intelligence could trigger two decades of economic and social upheaval, disrupting jobs and life even if the technology is managed successfully.

In an interview with the Decoder podcast posted Thursday, the Microsoft co-founder said the transition to an AI-driven economy would create winners and losers, potentially reshaping employment and raising questions about people's roles in society. [...] Gates said advances in AI and humanoid robotics could eventually allow machines to perform much of the physical labor carried out by humans, including building homes, growing food, and even performing surgery.

news.title: CPSC任命Beth Puchek为首席人工智能官（CAIO）

news.raw_snippet:
October 23, 2026

The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) today announced that Beth Puchek, who currently serves as the agency’s Chief Data Officer, has been appointed Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer (CAIO). She will lead the agency’s efforts to responsibly implement and govern super intelligence technologies in support of CPSC’s mission to protect consumers from unreasonable risks associated with consumer products.
